Source and verification code for the paper *Subexponential Weighted Counting and Exact Optimisation* by Deep Bhattacharjee.

The paper reproduces, with credit, the summation routine of OpenAI's preprint "The Exponential Time Hypothesis is False" (25 October 2026) for sparse formulas, and proves from it, with complete proofs, that the following are computed deterministically in time 2^{o(n)}: the whole weight profile of a sparse weighted constraint system (Max-k-SAT, Min-k-SAT, the count of optimal assignments), the number of satisfying assignments of each Hamming weight, Max-Cut and the maximum and minimum bisection of a sparse graph, the weighted independence polynomial of every graph (hence the independence and clique numbers and their counts), knapsack with an arbitrary conflict graph and several capacities, Vertex Cover in time 2^{o(k)} + poly(n), partition functions and homomorphism counts on bounded-degree graphs, the density of states of Ising and Potts systems with polynomially bounded couplings, dominating sets, matchings, hitting sets and sparse permanents, counting under a congruence, several linear statistics at once, Max-q-Cut and balanced partitions, f-factors, orientations, edge colourings and nowhere-zero flows on bounded-degree graphs, the Tutte polynomial on every hyperbola (x-1)(y-1) = q with q a positive integer, the weight enumerator, minimum distance and maximum-likelihood decoding of codes with sparse parity checks, bounded-degree hypergraphs, linear-size circuits, 0-1 and bounded integer programs with sparse rows (exact cover with bounded frequency, partially ordered knapsack), Max-Cut, Ising ground states, Max-k-SAT and sparse integer programs at average degree up to sqrt(log n)/(log log n)^3, k-SAT in SE and SNP ⊆ SE.

Version 1.2.0 adds independent sets under several budgets on every graph and the knapsack problem with a conflict graph (Theorem 6.10, Corollary 6.11), sparse integer programs (Theorem 7.17, Corollary 7.18), Max-k-SAT and integer programs at growing density (Corollary 7.21), and a seventh exact-arithmetic check.

Files: `subexponential-weighted-counting.pdf` (the paper), `subexponential-weighted-counting-tex.zip` (LaTeX source and figures), `subexponential-weighted-counting-arxiv.tar.gz` (arXiv-style source). The exact-arithmetic check program and its recorded output are in `code/`.
